metadata.name: Asri Store Design System
metadata.description: Visual design tokens, component appearance, interaction states, page patterns and responsive presentation rules synchronized with Asri Store App.json architecture V1.2.0.

uiReference.name: Storefront UI
uiReference.usage: Reference patterns only. Asri visual identity and this design system take precedence over library defaults.

brand: Create a modern, calm, polished and approachable fashion storefront.
Keep Asri's own visual identity; do not reproduce Storefront UI demos or another retailer's branding.
Use a restrained palette, clear hierarchy, generous whitespace and consistent component behavior.
Prioritize product imagery and purchase clarity over decorative UI.
productExperience: Mobile-first shopping experience with responsive enhancement for wider screens.
Make product discovery, product evaluation and checkout actions easy to understand.
Use consistent feedback for loading, success, validation, empty and error states.
Keep purchase-related information visible and unambiguous.
implementation: Tokens are the source of truth for visual values.
Components consume semantic tokens rather than arbitrary one-off values.
Visual presentation must remain separate from domain logic, data access and payment processing.
Storefront UI components may inform behavior and composition but must be adapted to Asri tokens.

avoid: Inconsistent radii, shadows or button treatments

rules: Use brand.primary for primary actions, selected controls and key interactive emphasis.
Use brand.secondary sparingly for promotions and supporting emphasis, not as a second primary action color.
Use semantic colors only for their matching status meaning.
Do not use color alone to communicate availability, payment or order status.
Do not introduce a new brand hue at component level without updating this token source.

fontFamily.sans: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, sans-serif

rules: Use Inter consistently across the storefront.
Use tabular numerals for prices, quantities and order identifiers where supported.
Avoid using font size alone to establish hierarchy; combine size, weight and spacing.
Use sentence case for interface labels.
Use the 4px base spacing scale.
Prefer consistent spacing tokens over arbitrary margins.
Keep dense product information readable with clear grouping.
Interactive controls must meet a 44px minimum target where practical.
Do not shrink icon-only controls below the minimum accessible target.
Keep the mobile storefront centered and readable on wider viewports.
Motion should clarify state changes and spatial transitions.
Avoid decorative or continuous motion.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion and provide a reduced-motion experience.
Canonical token references use tokens.<group>.<path>.
Short semantic aliases are allowed only when they resolve unambiguously to one canonical token.
Theme overrides use canonical token paths and must not create new token families.
All semantic tokens must resolve in every supported theme.
Do not hardcode light-theme colors in reusable components.
System theme follows the operating-system preference.
Theme overrides use canonical token paths relative to tokens, such as color.surface.page and color.brand.primary.default.
Unspecified theme values inherit from the base tokens; every semantic token must resolve in light, dark and system modes.

storefrontFrame.purpose: Constrain the actual mobile-first storefront canvas inside the wider viewport container.
rules: The mobile, tablet and desktop container widths describe the outer viewport container, not the storefront canvas.
The storefrontFrame is the inner application canvas and remains capped at 767px at every viewport width.
Center storefrontFrame within the outer container on tablet and desktop.
Do not stretch product cards or page content to the full 960px or 1280px outer container width.
Design and validate at 320px width before scaling up.
The primary storefront experience is mobile-first.
At wider widths, keep the mobile storefront constrained and centered rather than stretching product cards excessively.
Do not use 100vh or 100dvh as a required app-shell height token.
Use flexible layout sizing and natural document flow for page content.
Do not introduce horizontal page overflow.

page.maxWidthMeaning: Maximum width of the inner storefrontFrame, not the outer responsive viewport container.

rules: AppShell and StandalonePage are the two page layout families defined by App.json.
A route must use one page layout only.
BottomActionBar belongs to StandalonePage and remains in normal document flow.
BottomNavigation belongs to AppShell and must not be duplicated on StandalonePage.
Overlay is rendered independently of page layout.
The page maxWidth of 767px applies to the inner storefrontFrame; responsive.container breakpoints describe the outer viewport container.
Use one visually dominant primary action per context.
Do not use color alone to distinguish destructive actions.
Provide an accessible name.
Maintain a 44px target even when the visible icon is smaller.
Product image is the primary visual element.
Keep product title, current price and relevant availability easy to scan.
Do not show fabricated reviews, stock counts or discounts.
Do not let a long title cause inconsistent card heights.
Always pair status color with a readable status label.
Map only confirmed backend order states to visual statuses.
Use lucide-react icon names through the shared icon wrapper.
Icon-only actions must use IconButton with an accessible name.
Use semantic anchors for navigation.
Do not style navigation links as buttons unless they trigger an action.
Do not cause page-level horizontal overflow.
Preserve visible focus and touch scrolling.
QuickView is an overlay, not a route.
Use current product data only.
Provide a link or action to open ProductDetailPage for full details.
Use the same ProductCard specification across all grids.
Do not create placeholder product cards when data is unavailable.
Use approved campaign content and imagery only.
Do not imply an unapproved discount or promotion.
Use only sourced product data.
Do not fabricate stock, ratings, review counts or discounts.
Page patterns describe visual composition, not route definitions or business logic.
Follow App.json for page ownership and layout classification.
Only include BottomActionBar when a page has a primary action.
Do not duplicate header or navigation elements already provided by the active layout.
Every interactive element has hover, focus, active and disabled behavior where applicable.
Do not make essential actions depend on hover.
Use the interaction semantics of React components; do not copy Vue composables or APIs.
Use accessible state attributes such as aria-expanded, aria-selected and aria-invalid where appropriate.

disabled.mustExplain: when the reason is not self-evident

rules: Availability and physical stock are separate concepts.
Do not hide a product solely because its stock is zero unless application requirements explicitly say so.
Never invent stock quantities or availability states.
Payment visual status must reflect trusted backend state.
A browser return or redirect is not proof of successful payment.
Do not use a success state before backend confirmation.
Use clear, high-quality product photography.
Keep image aspect ratios consistent within the same product collection.
Do not distort product images.
Use a neutral image background where it improves product clarity.
Provide meaningful alt text for informative images.
Use one consistent icon family.
Use icons to support labels, not replace critical labels.
Use decorative icons with aria-hidden when they add no semantic information.
Do not mix unrelated icon libraries.

keyboard: All interactive elements are keyboard accessible.
Focus order follows the visual and semantic reading order.
Modal and drawer overlays trap focus when modal and restore focus on close.
touch: Minimum interactive target is 44px by 44px where practical.
Provide adequate spacing between adjacent touch controls.
semantics: Associate form labels and validation messages with inputs.
Expose dynamic status changes to assistive technology.
Do not communicate status by color alone.
motion: Do not rely on animation to communicate essential information.
content: Use clear and concise interface language.
Do not truncate critical price, payment or order status information.

contentGuidelines.language: Indonesian for customer-facing storefront copy unless a specific context requires otherwise
rules: Use consistent Indonesian terminology across pages.
Use explicit labels for price, shipping, discount and total.
Do not imply a discount unless a valid original and current price are available.
Avoid ambiguous labels for payment and order states.

tokenUsage: Map tokens to CSS custom properties.
Expose semantic tokens to Tailwind theme configuration.
Components must reference semantic tokens, not duplicate raw hex values.
Keep component visual variants centralized and typed in TypeScript.
Resolve component token aliases through tokens.referencePolicy; do not hardcode theme-specific colors.
Theme overrides use the canonical token paths declared in themes.tokenReferenceFormat.
rules: This file defines visual rules only; it does not define routes, component business logic, data fetching or payment logic.
App.json is the source of truth for application hierarchy and page classification.
design_system.json is the source of truth for tokens, component appearance and visual interaction states.
Do not install @storefront-ui/react solely because it is listed as a reference in App.json.
If a third-party component is adopted later, wrap or theme it to comply with Asri tokens and accessibility rules.
Every component in App.json BaseComponents must have a matching visual specification in components.
Every component in App.json CommerceBlocks must have a matching visual specification in blocks.
Every page in App.json page classification must have a matching pagePatterns entry.
Every App.json Overlay group must have a matching visual pattern and implementation mapping.
App.json names are architecture identifiers; implementation paths are code ownership locations.
BaseComponents map one-to-one to shared UI primitives unless a documented composition is required.
CommerceBlocks compose BaseComponents and map to reusable blocks.
FeatureComponents remain owned by their feature modules and are not promoted to shared components without review.
Overlay group names and overlay instances map to src/app/overlays and are not route definitions.

notAllowed: Copying Storefront UI default visual theme as Asri branding
Copying Vue implementation code into React
Allowing library defaults to override approved Asri tokens

changeControl: Preserve approved baseline tokens and component patterns.
Introduce future changes through semantic version increments.
Document token changes and component behavior changes in a changelog.
Do not change brand colors, typography or layout principles as incidental component styling.
Review visual changes against App.json before implementation.
Keep App.json architectureVersion and design_system.json metadata.architectureReference.version synchronized.
Keep component, block, page-pattern and overlay coverage synchronized with App.json.
Run the cross-file consistency checks before approving a version.

versionHistory.description: Previously approved Asri storefront design system baseline.
Expanded token coverage and mapped visual component and commerce-block rules to App.json V1.1.0 and Storefront UI V2 reference patterns.
Aligned component taxonomy, commerce blocks, page patterns, overlay mapping, responsive container semantics, token references and cross-file governance with App.json V1.2.0.

requiredChecks: Every AppShell and StandalonePage page has exactly one matching pagePatterns entry.
Every App.json BaseComponents item exists in design_system.json components.
Every App.json CommerceBlocks item exists in design_system.json blocks.
Every App.json Overlay group has a matching visual component and implementation mapping.
Every componentMapping target resolves to a defined component, block, or typography text style.
Every token reference resolves through canonical tokens or an explicit alias.
The page maxWidth is explicitly defined as the storefrontFrame width and is distinct from outer viewport container widths.
validation.note: The validation contract is specified here; this JSON update does not create the validator script.
